proposals.before: Late in Xiantong he took the jinshi degree and stayed in Chang'an; three years passed without his name on the rolls.
proposals.after: Late in Xiantong he sat the jinshi examination and stayed in Chang'an; three years passed without his name on the rolls.
proposals.reason: Chinese 舉進士 with 三歲不中第 means he sat for the exam and failed for three years, not that he obtained the degree.

proposals.before: At the end of Tang Xiantong he passed the jinshi examination and remained in Chang'an; three years he failed to place.
proposals.after: At the end of Tang Xiantong he sat the jinshi examination and remained in Chang'an; for three years he failed to place.
proposals.reason: 舉進士 here is candidacy/sitting, contradicted by 不中第; 'passed' is incorrect.

proposals.before: Si Maye, who styled himself Biaoren, came of a family from Wen in Henei.
proposals.after: Sima Ye, who styled himself Biaoren, came of a family from Wen in Henei.
proposals.reason: 司馬 is the compound surname Sima; 'Si Maye' wrongly splits it.

proposals.before: In Datong 2 he was made army inspector, helped Huo Cun retake Suzhou, and was memorialized Acting Minister of War.
proposals.after: In Dashun 2 he was made army inspector, helped Huo Cun retake Suzhou, and was memorialized Acting Minister of War.
proposals.reason: 大順 is Dashun (AD 890–891), not Datong.

proposals.before: Later he served on the staffs of the Xuanyi and Tianping commands.
proposals.after: Later he served on the staffs of the Xuanwu and Tianping commands.
proposals.reason: Chinese has 宣武, not 宣義; idiomatic wrongly uses Xuanyi.

proposals.before: At the Liang founding he became military commissioner of Huazhou with Acting Grand Guardian.
proposals.after: When the Founder received the mandate, he became military commissioner of Huazhou with Acting Grand Guardian.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits 太祖 as the actor of 受禪, collapsing it to an impersonal 'Liang founding' and losing the person reference present in the Chinese and literal.

proposals.before: An edict posthumously enfeoffed Palace Attendant.
proposals.after: An edict posthumously conferred Palace Attendant.
proposals.reason: 贈 of an office/title is posthumous conferral, not enfeoffment; 'enfeoffed' misrenders 贈侍中.

proposals.before: Cunjing had the merit of carrying the drum; Yanqing met the occasion of climbing the dragon scales; both became frontier defenders—also fitting!
proposals.after: Cunjin had the merit of carrying the drum; Yanqing met the occasion of climbing the dragon scales; both became frontier defenders—also fitting!
proposals.reason: Literal spells 存敬 as Cunjing while the chapter title and idiomatic use Cunjin; unify to the established English form.

decisions.reason: Focus unit has 舉進士…三歲不中第: 舉進士 is sitting for the examination, and 不中第 shows he did not place; 'took the jinshi degree' falsely asserts success. The proposed 'sat the jinshi examination' matches the Chinese and leaves the rest intact.
Same focus unit: 舉進士 is candidacy, contradicted by 不中第, so literal 'passed' is wrong. 'Sat' plus 'for three years he failed to place' restores the Chinese sense without inventing content.
Focus unit opens 司馬鄴; 司馬 is the compound surname Sima and 鄴 is Ye. 'Si Maye' wrongly splits the surname. Sima Ye is the correct personal name and the rest of the proposed sentence is accurate.
Focus unit dates the event 大順二年; 大順 is the Tang reign Dashun, not Datong (大同). Dashun matches the Chinese and leaves the remainder of the sentence intact.
Focus unit has 宣武、天平等軍; 宣武 is Xuanwu, not Xuanyi (宣義). The proposed replacement corrects the command name without other changes.

Focus unit begins 太祖受禪; the Founder is the explicit agent of receiving the abdication/mandate. 'At the Liang founding' erases that person reference. The proposed wording restores 太祖 as actor and matches the literal.
Focus unit is 詔贈侍中; 贈 of an office is posthumous conferral, not enfeoffment (封). 'Enfeoffed' misrenders the verb; 'conferred' matches 贈 and the already-correct idiomatic 'posthumously made'.

存敬 is the same person either way; Cunjing is a valid reading of 敬 (jìng). Changing only to match another English spelling is stylistic unification, not correction of a semantic or naming error in the Chinese sense.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0003 shows English Si Maye came only from wrongly splitting 司馬鄴; the personal-name claim must use Sima Ye while keeping zh, pinyin, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
Accepted r0003 shows English surname Si was produced by the split of compound 司馬; the surname claim must use Sima while keeping zh, pinyin, and the other claim fields.
Accepted r0003 shows English given name Maye absorbed part of the surname; the given-name claim must use Ye for 鄴 while keeping zh, pinyin, evidence, and the other claim fields.
